reviews.subject: w547/GAUSSIAN_BOUNDARY.md#C002
reviews.independent_reproduction: Angular averages of both sin^2 and cos^2 are pi; the radial 1/k term gives coefficient |G|^2/(4pi) log r. For p<2 the longitudinal spectral integral is L1 and tends to |G|^2 Lambda^(2-p)/(4pi(2-p)). Curl kills P_L and has density T/(4mu); disk integration gives Var(theta)=T Lambda^2/(16pi mu), hence the sixfold pair limit exp[-36 Var(theta)]=exp[-9T Lambda^2/(4pi mu)].
reviews.gap: No justified microscopic p(s) map; no free dislocations or actual bond-orientational observable.

reviews.subject: w547/GAUSSIAN_BOUNDARY.md#C003
reviews.scope: fixed-p Gaussian asymptotic and endpoint continuity
reviews.independent_reproduction: For p<2 the longitudinal term has a finite r->infinity limit, so its log-r coefficient is zero. At p=2 its coefficient is T|G|^2/(4pi a). For fixed r, 1-cos(k.re)=O(k^2) provides a p-independent integrable majorant near k=0, so p->2- can precede r->infinity. The iterated limits differ by T|G|^2/(4pi a)>0.
reviews.gap: This is a Gaussian endpoint warning, not a result about P0321's Riesz exponent s.
